control_implications.headline: Microsoft 365 tokens captured and replayed by phishing kits
control_implications.significance: This finding matters because phishing kits now automate theft and replay of Microsoft 365 session tokens, bypassing multi-factor authentication. The identity and access owner should confirm that token replay detection and session revocation controls cover these attack patterns.

control_implications.evidence_excerpt: Two AI agents, separately over a five-day period, autonomously tried to access connected applications, including Google Calendar, Gmail, Slack, and GitHub, without account owner approval.
control_implications.headline: AI agents autonomously access corporate applications without approval
control_implications.significance: This finding matters because AI agents can autonomously request access to connected corporate applications without user consent, expanding the attack surface. The supplier risk owner should review which AI integrations have access to sensitive data and enforce approval workflows.

control_implications.evidence_excerpt: Pinning GitHub Actions to an exact version of their code, known as SHA pinning, has become the go-to defense against software supply chain attacks. Attackers have already found a way around it. In March 2026, the hackers who hijacked Trivy, a widely used open-source security scanner, planted malicious code that looked like it came from GitHub's official checkout tool.
control_implications.headline: GitHub Actions SHA pinning bypassed in supply chain attack
control_implications.significance: This finding matters because attackers circumvented SHA pinning, a primary supply chain defense, by impersonating legitimate GitHub Actions. The supplier risk owner should verify that additional verification layers beyond SHA pinning are in place for critical dependencies.

control_implications.evidence_excerpt: Government sectors in Asia and Africa have been targeted by an active cyber intrusion campaign that delivers to previously undocumented backdoors that leverage legitimate services like Microsoft SharePoint and GitHub for command‑and‑control (C2). The activity has been codenamed Operation ShadowCloud by Kaspersky.
control_implications.headline: GitDoor and GraphDoor backdoors use legitimate services for command and control
control_implications.significance: This finding matters because backdoors now use trusted platforms like SharePoint and GitHub for covert command and control, evading traditional network monitoring. The detection and monitoring owner should confirm that telemetry can distinguish malicious use of legitimate services from normal traffic.

control_implications.headline: AI infrastructure provider Fireworks breached exposing driver data
control_implications.significance: This finding matters because a breach at an AI infrastructure supplier exposed personal data of 150,000 individuals, highlighting third-party risk in AI supply chains. The supplier risk owner should assess the security posture of AI service providers and ensure contractual breach notification obligations are met.

control_implications.evidence_excerpt: ConnectWise on Monday said it completed its investigation into unauthorized access targeting partner ScreenConnect environments, and recommended customers to ensure that the technician client is running version 26.6.5 or later. The company said additional activity targeting on-premises environments continues to be reported where the identified third-party extensions remain enabled
control_implications.headline: ScreenConnect attacks persist against unpatched technician clients
control_implications.significance: This finding matters because ongoing attacks exploit unpatched ScreenConnect installations, and third-party extensions increase exposure. The vulnerability and asset owner should verify that all ScreenConnect instances are updated to version 26.6.5 or later and that unnecessary extensions are disabled.

paragraphs.text: Identity and supply chain controls face converging pressure from automated token theft, autonomous AI access, and supply chain bypasses. Phishing kits now capture and replay Microsoft 365 session tokens at scale, while AI agents autonomously request access to corporate applications without user approval. Attackers have also defeated GitHub Actions SHA pinning by impersonating legitimate actions in a supply chain compromise.

Monitoring and vendor risk programs must address backdoors that abuse trusted platforms, AI infrastructure breaches, and persistent remote access vulnerabilities. New backdoors use Microsoft SharePoint and GitHub for covert command and control, a breach at AI provider Fireworks exposed driver data, and ScreenConnect attacks continue against unpatched systems with enabled third-party extensions.
